title: Principal opens of finite product spectra
statement: Let H be a commutative ring, h∈H, m a natural number, and F_i a family of commutative H-algebras indexed by Fin m. Put B=Π_i F_i, U_i=D(algebraMap H F_i h) in Spec F_i, and V=D(algebraMap H B h) in Spec B. There exists an isomorphism e:∐_i U_i≅V such that e.hom followed by V→Spec B→Spec H is the coproduct of the maps U_i→Spec F_i→Spec H. This includes m=0 and zero component rings.

source.place: Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Limits: sigmaSpec, ι_sigmaSpec and its finite IsIso instance; Stacks Tag 01I1

proof.text:
the evaluation maps give sigmaSpec, which is an isomorphism for a finite
index set. The inverse image of D(h) under each evaluation is D(h_i), because
prime-spectrum comap takes basic opens to basic opens. Restrict sigmaSpec to this
open. Restriction commutes with disjoint union, so the restricted source is the
coproduct of the component basic opens. This gives the isomorphism e. Composing
with the open inclusion gives the coproduct of component inclusions followed by
the evaluation maps. Composing further with Spec of the diagonal H-algebra map
reduces each summand to its structural map, giving the equation by Sigma.hom_ext.
The empty-index case follows from sigmaSpec for the zero ring.
